name: Trauma-Informed Content: Creating Resilient Experiences
description:
What does it mean to create content that still works when users are stressed, overwhelmed, or navigating difficult circumstances? In *Trauma-Informed Content: Creating Resilient Experiences*, Megan Legawiec introduces a practical framework for designing with safety, trust, choice, control, flexibility, and context in mind. Through real-world examples and a sample stress test, she’ll show how trauma can affect comprehension, decision-making, trust, and task completion, and how content teams can respond. The session also explores how changing social and organizational contexts can affect the assumptions built into our experiences, and how thoughtful governance can help teams keep those experiences resilient over time. You’ll leave with questions, principles, and practical steps you can bring into your work right away.

**About the speaker:** Megan Legawiec is a UX writer and content designer with a passion for crafting inclusive, accessible, and trauma-informed digital experiences. Before transitioning into tech, she spent over a decade teaching secondary social studies, where she honed her skills in communication, empathy, and designing for diverse needs. Today, Megan brings that same human-centered mindset to her work in UX. She shapes content that meets users where they are and builds meaningful connections. Her experience spans startups to enterprise settings, always grounded in clarity, compassion, and inclusion.

3 platform requirements for agentic engineering
description:
Agentic engineering only works if the platform underneath it can support autonomous action safely. Justin Billig and Dan Rye, co-founders of Tensure, break down the three platform capabilities engineering organizations need to move agents out of experimentation and into production: a controlled action layer, identity and guardrails, and a feedback loop.

**You'll come away knowing:**

1. How to build a controlled action layer that exposes approved capabilities to agents through APIs, Infrastructure as Code, and GitOps rather than direct infrastructure access.

**Zoom link:** [https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/82308186562)
Join us for two deep dives into hidden AI performance costs: surprise PyTorch recompilations during inference and compute, memory, and communication bottlenecks in Jev training.
**Talk #0: Introductions and Meetup Updates**
by Chris Fregly and Antje Barth
**Talk #1: Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads**
by Chaim Rand
`torch.compile` can accelerate steady-state inference, yet a guard failure on a new input shape or layout can trigger an expensive recompilation in the request path. Drawing on his latest post, Chaim will compare six approaches using a dynamic graph-neural-network example: cache preloading, bounded recompilation with eager fallback, Dynamo and input-layout tuning, warmup seeding, background compilation, and ahead-of-time compilation with `torch.export` and AOTInductor. He’ll explain their tradeoffs and how the right choice depends on the model, input distribution, runtime environment, and latency requirements.
**Bio:** Chaim Rand is a machine-learning algorithm developer who writes about PyTorch and practical AI/ML performance optimization.
**Based on:** [Overcoming the PyTorch Recompilation Dilemma in Real-Time Inference Workloads](https://chaimrand.medium.com/overcoming-the-pytorch-recompilation-dilemma-in-real-time-inference-workloads-069fac5485cd)
**Talk #2: From Profiles to Throughput: How TypeSafe Optimized Jev with Zymtrace**
by Israel Ogbole, Co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace
Israel will explore the latest Zymtrace/TypeSafe case study on training and serving Jev. He’ll discuss how continuous CPU/GPU profiling and MCP-accessible profile data supported an iterative optimization loop across compute, memory, communication, and inference synchronization. The published case study reports approximately 46% higher training throughput on the same hardware after three successive changes, plus approximately 10% better inference performance after removing a hidden device-to-host synchronization. The talk will focus on how the team found each bottleneck, measured each change, and identified the next constraint.
**Bio:** Israel Ogbole is co-founder and CEO of Zymtrace, which develops continuous CPU/GPU profiling tools for performance optimization.
**Based on:** [How TypeSafe achieved 46% higher GPU throughput training Jev — with the help of Zymtrace](https://zymtrace.com/article/typesafe-zymtrace/)

Many of our patrons advised us that they have a Pop-up Blocker on their iPhones and it hinders them from buying tickets. To unblock, please follow the following steps :

1\. Go to Settings\.
2\. Scroll down to Safari and click on it\.

1\. Open Google Chrome\.
2\. Click on the three dots and you will see many options\.
3\. Click on Settings\.
